recipe_name: Root Vegetable Salad with Tahini Dressing
creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Ingredients: Yucca, white sweet potatoes, one potato (all steamed in Instant Pot). Frozen (thawed) edamame, Persian cucumbers. Dressing: Tahini, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, coconut aminos, and hot sauce. Method: Steam the root vegetables in an Instant Pot. Add thawed edamame and Persian cucumbers. Dress with a mixture of tahini, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, coconut aminos, and hot sauce.

creator: Group Member
text: Brands like Califia Farms (unsweetened organic), Malk Organics (unsweetened), Three Trees (original or vanilla bean), and Elmhurst (unsweetened) are often recommended for their simple ingredient lists.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared a resource for veggie rolls with rice paper: https://thankful2plants.com/recipes/recipe-class-veggie-rolls-boats.html. He also suggested using brown rice paper instead of regular rice paper, providing an Amazon link for brown rice paper: https://www.amazon.com/s?k=brown+rice+paper.

creator: Group Member
text: A group member shared an oil-free method for cooking taro, stating it tastes 'way better than fried version with oil'. Even their kid agreed it tastes better than the fried version. This suggests an oil-free baking or air-frying method for taro, though the exact technique was not detailed in the chat.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared a comprehensive collection of over 2,000 Whole Food Plant-Based recipe cards available at https://thankful2plants.com/recipes/. The collection includes categories like Sweet Porridge & Desserts (Oatmeal, Beyond Oatmeal, Desserts), Indian Meal Prep (Idli, Dosa, Roti Paratha, Khichdi, Umpa, Pulao, Pongal, Dal, Sambhar, Rasam, Sabzi, Bhaji, Poriyal, Side Dishes, Rainbow Veggie Medley, Yogurt, Raita, Spice Mixes), Soups, Salads, Sandwiches (Soups, Stews, Salads, Sandwiches & Pita Pockets, Hummus, Tofu, Tempeh), Noodles, Burgers, Pancakes, Snacks (Noodles & Pasta, Tikkis, Cutlets, Falafel, Dumplings, Savory Pancakes & Waffles, Savory Snacks), Masala & Chutneys (Chutneys, Dips, Dressings, Sauces, Spreads), Smoothies & Beverages, and Meal Inspiration (Rainbow Meals, Indian Thali). Links to Google Photo albums for each category were also provided.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet recommended an Electric food processor vegetable chopper (BUMET brand, 500W, 2x8cup bowls, 2 bi-layer 4 blades) for everyday salad cutting, mincing, and pureeing. He mentioned it's easy to use, clean, and efficient, though he hasn't personally used this specific model. (Link: https://a.co/d/9gtZDBq)

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared a 2-minute YouTube video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pu1d759g8E4) on how to eat fresh green almonds, after a group member inquired about them.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Ingredients: 8-10 raw dates, 7-8 regular dates (deseeded, soaked in water), 1 Tbsp golden berries (tart, soaked; if not available, add 1 Tbsp raw mango), 1 tsp black pepper, 0.5 tsp cinnamon, 0.5 tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp vinegar, 1 tsp lemon, 1 tsp amchoor powder (raw mango powder). Method: Adjust quantities of black pepper and tart ingredients (golden berries, raw mango, raw mango powder, lemon) according to taste. This chutney is described as unique, tangy, and sweet.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Method: Wet two rice papers and place them one on top of the other, smoothing out any creases and bumps. Use a sharp-edged 'katori' bowl to cut out circular shapes. Place them in an air fryer. The paper will puff up like puris.

creator: Ashwini Vikram
text: Ingredients: Grated carrots, beetroot, and green bell pepper (sautéed before adding to batter). Batter: Overnight soaked split yellow Moong dal, ground with ginger, Jeera, green chilies, curry leaves, and salt (implied WFPB compliant, so minimal or no added salt). Method: Sauté the grated vegetables. Prepare the batter by grinding the soaked moong dal with the spices. Combine the sautéed vegetables with the batter and cook as savory pancakes or dosa. A group member also mentioned using green moong dal soaked overnight for a similar breakfast.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 1.5 cups Amaranth (soaked overnight), 4 Tbsp Date paste, 2 powdered Cardamom, 1.5 cups Soy milk, 2 cups Water, 0.5 cup Mango pulp, 1 Tbsp Almond butter, 10-12 Makhanna, 2 Figs, Dry fruits (for garnish), Fresh fruits (e.g., mango, peaches, plums), Raisins, Dried cherries. Method: Put all ingredients except mango pulp and garnishing into an Instant Pot. Pressure cook for 20 minutes. After pressure is released, add mango pulp, stir, and adjust sweetness. Dish out and garnish with toppings. Gurmeet noted using a store-bought date paste with only dates as an ingredient.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku clarified that organic noodles can be used if they are made from whole grains, not polished grains. Examples of compliant noodles include buckwheat noodles (soba), whole wheat noodles, or brown rice noodles. Non-compliant noodles to avoid are glass noodles (made from starch extracts) and typical rice noodles (made from polished white rice). The tip is to always check the ingredient list for whole grains versus polished grains or starch extracts.

recipe_name: Travel Cooking Hack with Dehydrated Veggies and Dal
creator: Group Member
text: For travel without kitchen access, a member shared a creative hack: they powdered toor dal at home, added tadka, tomato powder, garlic powder, onion powder, spices, and dehydrated veggies. This mix was then cooked in an Instant Pot (carried along) and served with pre-cooked brown rice packets. This method turned out delicious and is useful for creating easy-to-prep compliant recipes while traveling.

creator: Group Member
text: Ingredients: Barley, soy curls (compliant as they only contain soybeans), a lot of cabbage, miso, water, smoked paprika, dill, caraway, pepper. Optional additions: a few juniper berries, bay leaves, and peppers or tomatoes (if no nightshade preference). Method: Combine all ingredients in an Instant Pot. Cook for 25 minutes on high pressure, followed by natural release. The creator noted it 'doesn't look so great but tastes awesome'.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Ingredients: Boiled split toor dal, 1 spoon pickle masala, coriander powder, grated ginger, turmeric powder, salt (implied WFPB compliant), sweetener (date paste or syrup as substitute for jaggery), kokum (as souring agent, or tomatoes). Tadka: Whole red chili, curry leaves, mustard seeds, jeera, hing. Garnish with fresh cilantro. This recipe is for regular split toor dal.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Ingredients: Whole toor dal (soaked overnight, boiled nicely to a soft consistency in a pressure cooker), onions, garlic, green chili paste, red chili powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, little garam masala, salt (implied WFPB compliant), tomatoes or kokum (as souring agent). Method: For seasoning, sauté onions, add garlic and green chili paste and sauté until raw smell goes away. Add all powder spices and salt. Let it boil nicely until desired consistency. Kusum mentioned her mum used to add lots of garlic. This dal is widely used in Baroda.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku provided two methods for making oil-free idli: 1. Using Silicone Idli Liners (available on Amazon and other retailers). 2. The 'Cloth Technique': cutting cotton cloth into a circular shape with a hole in the center to easily remove idli from the maker. Commercially sold cotton/muslin products for idli making are also available.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared a link to a long list of SOS-Free (without Salt, Oil & Sugar) WFPB products maintained by the NHA (National Health Association), USA: https://www.healthscience.org/health-science/sos-free-products/. The NHA has advocated the SOS-Free WFPB lifestyle since 1948.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Ingredients: 1 small brinjal (sliced into small pieces). Batter: 2 Tbsp besan (chickpea flour), 0.5 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp amchoor, 1 tsp Pancha Phoron spice mix (ground), 1 tsp crushed garlic, 1 tsp dried kasoori methi, a pinch of ajwain (carom seeds, rubbed between fingers), 2 tsp chopped cilantro (coriander leaves). Optional: minced green chili or chili flakes. Method: 1. Mix batter ingredients, adding water 1 tsp at a time to form a batter that is neither too hard nor too runny. 2. Coat brinjal slices with the batter on all sides. 3. Air fry for 10 minutes per side at 180°C. 4. Serve with green chutney, date chutney, lemon, and favorite spice mixes (e.g., Chaat Masala).

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet shared an impromptu recipe for Peanut Ridgegourd Chutney. The idea came from having ridgegourd on the counter and deciding to add it to a peanut chutney being made for idlis. The specific ingredients and method for the peanut chutney base are not detailed, but the key is the addition of ridgegourd to a standard peanut chutney.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared that black rice is cooked just like regular brown rice: soak overnight, then three whistles in a pressure cooker.

recipe_name: Sugar-Free, Flourless Oatmeal, Apple, and Carrot Bake
creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Ingredients: 2 cups (200g) rolled oats (chopped in a blender), 1 tsp baking powder, 1 cup (240ml) plant-based milk, 1 grated carrot, 9 dried apricots (rinsed with hot water and chopped), 4 Tbsp raisins (rinsed with hot water), 1 grated apple. Optional additions: 1 tsp cinnamon, 0.5 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt, 1-2 Tbsp chia seeds or flaxseed meal. Instructions: 1. Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). 2. Prepare Oats: Blend rolled oats briefly to a coarse flour/fine flakes consistency. Combine with baking powder (and optional salt/spices). 3. Mix Wet Ingredients: In another bowl, mix grated carrot, grated apple, milk, chopped apricots, and raisins. Let sit for 5-10 minutes. 4. Combine Everything: Mix wet and dry ingredients. Add more milk if too dry. 5. Pour into Baking Dish: Use a small baking dish or loaf pan (lined with parchment). Flatten top. 6. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until set and lightly golden (toothpick comes out mostly clean). 7. Cool for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. Storage: Store in fridge up to 5 days, freezes well. Serve as breakfast bar, snack, or healthy dessert.

creator: Group Member
text: A group member suggested exploring local berries in India, which might be healthier than popular Western ones. Amla is highlighted as the healthiest berry. The member also shared an experience with 'black tomato' berries (identified as black nightshade) growing as a weed in their garden, which they found delicious and healthy, despite not liking regular tomatoes. These berries are fragile and cannot be stored or transported.

creator: Multiple Group Members
text: Several ideas were shared for using jackfruit seeds: roasted seeds as a snack, boiled with garlic + red chili chutney, making sabzi like potatoes (chop into 2, sauté onions, haldi, mirchi, then add seeds), sprouted seeds, making 'Bikkand (seeds) sukke', 'bikkand saung', adding to chana for 'ghashi', or making a dry potato-like subzi. A link to a Jackfruit Seed Hummus recipe (https://jollytomato.com/jackfruit-seed-hummus-recipe/) was also shared, with a suggestion to try it without EVOO. Tips for dry roasting include using a pan on the stove (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zINtWlD4cDI) or an air fryer (https://www.youtube.com/shorts/iq0OeLKUqyY), skipping salt or oil. When air frying, it was noted that seeds tend to fly around, so placing them between racks or under a cover is recommended.

creator: Group Member
text: For those who don't do well with cilantro, a member suggested buying various sprouts from farmers markets to use as a garnish instead. These add visual appeal and different flavors, serving as a good alternative.

creator: Uma Venkataraman WFPB
text: Uma Venkataraman WFPB suggested leaving some of the peel in bananas when preparing them, as it is one of the best parts and is loaded with fiber.

creator: Group Member
text: A member shared a recipe for Avocado Kulfi, noting that blending avocado quickly with other ingredients and freezing prevents oxidation, resulting in a nice green kulfi. They suggested switching or adding different fruits/berries like mango, strawberry, or cherry for variety. Initial recipe used Oatly, but it was noted that Oatly often contains added oils and is not WFPB compliant. Suggestions for WFPB alternatives included Eden Soy (soybeans and water only) or using water-soaked organic rolled oats for body. The member planned to try these alternatives.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Ingredients: Dry ingredients: Jowar flour, chana flour, ragi flour in a 4:3:3 ratio (total ~100g for 25 biscuits), 1 tsp baking soda, 10g each cocoa powder and carob powder (adjust for desired darkness). Wet ingredients: Cashew milk (homemade), 8-10 dates (blended with milk, adjust for sweetness). Method: 1. Blend dates with cashew milk to make a sweet milk. 2. Use this milk to make a soft, non-sticky dough with the dry ingredients. 3. Roll out the dough and cut into desired shapes. 4. Make impressions with a chopstick (like Hide and Seek biscuits). 5. Press some dark chocolate chips onto the biscuits. 6. Bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes. Kids loved them as a good alternative to chocolate and biscuits.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared that whisking the ground moong dal batter for a few minutes with a fork was helpful in making Idli somewhat fluffy, without the need for Eno.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku shared six ideas to reduce or eliminate salt in meals, emphasizing that salt is 'The Lazy Man's way of flavoring meals' and that reducing it allows one to taste other subtleties. 1. Naturally high acidic foods: lemon, vinegars. 2. Salt-free mustard. 3. Vegetables with naturally higher sodium: celery, broccoli. 4. Naturally spicy foods: cayenne pepper, chipotle pepper, berbere spice mix, red pepper flakes, jalapenos, chile peppers, ginger. 5. Herbs & dried spices: onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper, minced garlic, fresh onion, thyme, oregano, basil, paprika, cumin, rosemary, mint (fresh or dried). 6. Sea vegetables (nori, dulse) and veggie stock. A follow-up discussion clarified that some non-whole foods like cacao powder, tofu, tempeh, plant-based milks, teas, veggie broth, and vegetable juices are often considered acceptable in WFPB circles, despite not being strictly 'whole'.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Gunjan Sahni WFPB shared two frosting recipes for a cake: White frosting: Cashew, tofu, raisins. Pink frosting: Sweet potato, dates, beetroot, peanut butter. She also mentioned making sprinkles from coconut flour mixed with beetroot puree (for pink) and coconut flour mixed with a pinch of turmeric and water (for yellow), which kids enjoyed adding.

creator: Kusum WFPB
text: Kusum WFPB shared a link to a vegan Mishti Doi recipe: https://holycowvegan.net/vegan-mishti-doi/.

creator: Shalini Other Lady WFPB
text: Shalini Other Lady WFPB shared modifications for the Plant-Based Mango Cheesecake recipe from Seonkyoung Longest (https://seonkyounglongest.com/plant-based-mango-cheesecake/): The crust does not need maple syrup, and roasted almond flour was used in the base. For the 'cheese' part, coconut cream was reduced to one can and silken tofu was added instead. While maple syrup was used for a non-WFPB group, date syrup would be preferred for WFPB. For the mango layer, 1/2 frozen Kesar mango pulp and 1/2 Kent mangoes were used. Quantities were increased for a larger cake.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 5 Tbsp Ragi, 1.5 cups Water, 1 cup Soy milk, 1.5 Tbsp Almond flour, 3 powdered Cardamom, 3 Tbsp Date syrup, 3 Tbsp Date sugar, Cashews (to garnish). Method: 1. Add ragi and water to a pot, mix well. 2. Place on stove, bring to a gentle boil on slow to medium heat while whisking continuously. 3. Add remaining ingredients (soy milk, almond flour, cardamom, date syrup, date sugar) and continue stirring until the mix thickens and turns shiny (approx. 25-30 minutes). The consistency should be like idli batter. Adjust sweetness to taste. 4. Pour into a 2-3 inch deep container (e.g., bread baking tray). 5. Refrigerate for 2-3 hours. 6. Loosen edges with a knife, invert onto a plate, cut into squares, and garnish with cashew bits. Keep refrigerated. This is a WFPB version of a traditional dessert, originally made with coconut milk.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet shared tips for popping amaranth: Use a medium hot pot. Try popping no more than one tablespoon of amaranth at a time. Play with the temperature to find the right heat for popping. If the pot is too hot, the amaranth may burn instead of popping. A specific brand, Anna and Sarah Amaranth (https://a.co/d/ik3vKMT), was recommended as one that pops well. Another member mentioned doing the same with quinoa.

creator: Gurmeet Singh Manku
text: Gurmeet Singh Manku initiated a discussion on WFPB-compliant coconut substitutes, as coconuts are discouraged by some WFPB luminaries. Members shared ideas: Sharmila Vedam suggested grinding silken tofu with 1-2 Tbsp of coconut (for flavor) for South Indian gravies. Padma suggested grinding a tiny amount of coconut for flavor with roasted daliya for similar taste and texture. Uma Venkataraman WFPB noted fig leaves have a hint of young coconut flavor and can be used to wrap food or in desserts. Ambika suggested celery (plus hemp or cashews) as a substitute in koottu, chutneys, and pachadis, and soaked raw peanuts for 'morekuzhambu'. Ambika also advised adding soaked chia seeds while blending to mask the flavor of coconut substitutes and gradually reducing coconut until the right taste is achieved. Links to Facebook group discussions on coconut substitutes were also provided.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: 2 cups popped amaranth (plus extra for rolling), 10-12 dates (soaked in ~4 Tbsp warm water), 4 Tbsp roasted peanuts, 2 Tbsp dried sweet cherries, 0.5 cup soy milk, 2 tsp almond flour. Method: 1. In a blender, combine soaked dates (with soaking water), cherries, peanuts, and half of the soy milk. Blend to a thick paste, adding more milk in batches as needed. 2. Transfer the paste to a mixing bowl. Add popped amaranth and almond flour, mix well to form a cohesive, chapati-consistency dough. 3. Wet palms with a little water, roll the mixture into ladoos. 4. Roll the ladoos in extra popped amaranth. Ladoos are ready to enjoy.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Ingredients: Lemon, 21 Salute seasoning, dried oregano, dried basil, sumac. Optional additions: apple cider vinegar, peach cider vinegar. This dressing is used for zucchini and described as 'yum and so satisfying'.

creator: Gurmeet
text: Gurmeet discussed vegetable options for a Vegetable Korma, stating that any available vegetables like mushrooms, zucchini, bell peppers, or broccoli can be used. The typical 'must-haves' are potatoes, carrots, peas, and cauliflower. This was in response to a question about replacing Brussels sprouts with cabbage in an Indian dish.

creator: Gunjan Sahni WFPB
text: Ingredients: Date paste, imli (tamarind), curry leaves, green chili, mustard seeds, hing (asafoetida). Method: All ingredients are added to boiling water and then poured over the dhokla. This tadka is oil-free and gives a nice flavor and glistening appearance.

creator: Shruti Mirashi Joshi
text: Shruti Mirashi Joshi recommended WFPB Chef Neelima Sriram on Instagram (https://www.instagram.com/chefneelimasriram?igsh=OWk1eGE4b3Fha3Y2) for interesting recipes.
